title: Measurement of Time and Motion
seo_title: Measurement of Time and Motion Class 7 Science Worksheet (NCERT Curiosity Ch 8)
standard_code: Class 7, Curiosity Chapter 8: Measurement of Time and Motion
standard_text: Measuring time: sundials, water clocks, sand clocks, pendulum and quartz clocks; the simple pendulum and its time period; the SI unit of time; speed, units of speed and average speed; uniform and non-uniform motion; distance–time graphs (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 8).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 7 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 8: ancient and modern clocks, the simple pendulum and its time period, speed = distance ÷ time, km/h and m/s, and uniform and non-uniform motion. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Time period = total time ÷ number of oscillations.
body_html:
How to think about it

People measured time with sundials, water clocks (ghatika) and hourglasses; today we use pendulum, quartz and atomic clocks. The SI unit of time is the second. One oscillation of a pendulum is a full swing to one side and back; the time for one oscillation is its time period, which depends on the length of the string, not on the mass of the bob.

Speed is the distance travelled per unit time: speed = distance ÷ time, in m/s or km/h (1 m/s = 3.6 km/h). Motion with a constant speed in a straight line is uniform; motion with changing speed is non-uniform. On a distance–time graph, a steeper line means a higher speed.

Example

A bus covers 120 km in 2 h. Speed?

120 ÷ 2

Answer: 60 km/h

Example

20 oscillations in 30 s. Time period?

30 ÷ 20

Answer: 1.5 s

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying distance and time to get speed.
  • Timing just one swing of a pendulum.
  • Thinking a heavier bob swings faster.

faq.q: What is the time period of a pendulum?
faq.a: The time taken for one complete oscillation; it depends on the length of the pendulum.

faq.q: What is the difference between uniform and non-uniform motion?
faq.a: In uniform motion an object covers equal distances in equal times; in non-uniform motion its speed changes.

c: showing the time of day by the shadow of a stick or a raised edge
keeping time by the very regular vibrations of a quartz crystal

items.e: A quartz clock: keeping time by the very regular vibrations of a quartz crystal.

items.q: A pendulum makes 50 oscillations in 125 seconds. What is its time period?
items.e: Time period = total time ÷ number of oscillations = 125 ÷ 50 = 2.5 s.

items.q: A pendulum makes 40 oscillations in 100 seconds. What is its time period?
items.e: Time period = total time ÷ number of oscillations = 100 ÷ 40 = 2.5 s.

items.q: What is the SI unit of speed?
A pendulum has a time period of 1.5 s. How long does it take to make 10 oscillations?
A pendulum makes 10 oscillations in 12 seconds. What is its time period?
items.e: Time period = total time ÷ number of oscillations = 12 ÷ 10 = 1.2 s.

items.q: Does the time period of a pendulum change if a heavier bob is used (same length)?
c: no, it stays nearly the same

items.q: Which of these is an example of uniform motion?

items.e: An escalator carrying people up: uniform motion.

items.e: A car slowing down at a red light: not uniform motion. The other three are.
